EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A persistent, slow-moving trough remained over the American Samoa islands between March 26 and March 30. WFO American Samoa recorded a total of 5.45 inches of rainfall during this time. This led to saturated soils that triggered multiple landslides across the territory.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A landslide was reported at Poloa Village on the morning of March 30, scattering debris and rocks across the main road. No injuries were reported.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A thunderstorm moved over Tutuila island on the morning of May 20th. Gusty winds accompanied heavy rainfall. The highest estimated winds are on the western edge of the island where structural damage and flying debris were reported. WFO American Samoa recorded 1.53 inches of rainfall between 4 AM and 5 AM.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: An NWS Employee reported gusty winds that occurred during a thunderstorm in Amanave village that uprooted trees, tore off the roof of traditional Samoan kitchen hut, broke an electrical pole leading to power outages, and moved a dumpster about 20 feet away from it's original location. Pictures also show debris scattered across the village. Wind speed estimated by reviewing damage. Monetary damage is estimated.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong high pressure system centered to the south of Fiji moved a trough from the south of American Samoa onto the territorial islands on May 16th through the 18th. This stationary weather pattern lead to over 9.68 inches of rain recorded at WFO American Samoa. This includes 3.55 inches that fell in two hours on the afternoon of the 18th. This intense rainfall led to widespread flash flooding throughout the territory. Multiple landslides were also reported due to the intense rainfall on saturated soils.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A social media post shows flash flooding from heavy rainfall during the afternoon of the 18th in Malaeloa Village. Pictures show significant overflow from Fuafua stream. Monetary damage is estimated.
